A gentle, respectful retelling of Luke 2 and Matthew 2 for church groups, Sunday school classes, family gatherings and small groups. The story is the fun: everyone listens for the cue words and the gifts travel around the circle.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Sit in a circle, each holding one wrapped gift. One person reads a story aloud.
2. On LEFT pass your gift to the player on your left, on RIGHT pass it to your right, and on ACROSS swap gifts with the player opposite you.
3. When the story ends, keep the gift in your hands and open it on a count of three.

WHAT'S INCLUDED
4 PDF files, 14 pages each: US Letter and A4, each in full color and in a low-ink version (the art as outlines only).
- Page 1, Cover and how to play: 3 lines of instructions and a list of every page

- Pages 5-6, The Shepherds and the Good News: the shepherds' night, about 3 minutes, any group size, 17 cues (9 LEFT, 8 RIGHT)
- Pages 7-8, A Baby in Bethlehem: large print for ages 5 to 10, about 3 minutes, any group size, 12 cues (7 LEFT, 5 RIGHT)

PLAYERS AND TIME
4 to 30 players. The full story uses ACROSS, so it needs an even circle: the host can join in with a spare gift. The short story and the kids' story use only LEFT and RIGHT, so any number of players from 4 to 30 works. Times are estimates: reading aloud plus time for the group to pass.

FROM THE GOSPELS
The retelling follows Luke 2 and Matthew 2 in original words. The few lines in quotation marks from the angel, the angels' praise and the wise men's question are from the King James Version, which is in the public domain. The Bible gives no number of wise men, so the stories give none. The words LEFT, RIGHT and ACROSS are game cues, not part of the Bible account. The stories themselves contain no prayer. The closing prayer is optional and sits on its own page, so you can leave it out when you print.

Designed by Cedar Loom Prints using digital design tools, including AI-assisted ones. Files are checked before listing.
